csv_project_name: DOER Clean Energy Grant Program Feasibility Studies
csv_scope_of_work: The Massachusetts Department of Energy Resources (DOER) develops and implements policies and programs to ensure the adequacy, security, diversity, and cost-effectiveness of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts energy supply to create a clean, affordable, equitable, and resilient energy future. Clean energy feasibility studies may investigate any number of technology, equipment, and/or material options that are designed to reduce or eliminate the use of onsite fossil fuels, reduce energy use and/or costs, and advance the development and installation of clean and renewable energy resources. The DOER funds shall only be made available for studies that examine options related to non-fossil fuels that support efforts to meet LBE energy and emissions reduction targets. Studies may look at any combination of strategies/technologies, including but not limited to: 1. Renewable thermal applications, including: Heat pumps (ground-, air-, and water-source) Clean modern wood heating systems Solar thermal Advanced biofuels 2. Innovative solar applications Innovative solar applications include new solar technologies or techniques that have not yet been widely adopted paired with energy storage/peak demand reduction, building electrification, grid interactive efficient buildings, and/or electric vehicle charging. 3. Combined heat and power systems utilizing renewable fuels. 4. Energy resilience utilizing clean energy resources. 5. Energy storage, including, but not limited to: Battery storage Compressed air storage Fuel cells Thermal energy storage systems 6. Long-range building, campus- or facility-wide decarbonization studies. 7. Other clean technologies and/or strategies that target reductions in energy use, emissions, and fossil fuels (applicants must provide a detailed description of the potential associated energy and environmental benefits).
csv_disciplines_requested: Feasibility Studies, Electrical Engineering, Energy Engineering
